title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers where technical or scientific knowledge is required in such areas as biology, engineering, chemistry, and electronics, normally obtained from at least 2 years of postsecondary education.

tasks.text: Sell service contracts for technical or scientific products.
Contact new or existing customers to discuss how specific products or services can meet their needs.
Demonstrate the operation or use of technical or scientific products.
Sell technical and scientific products that are environmentally sound or designed for environmental remediation.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Select or assist customers in selecting products based on customer needs, product specifications, and applicable regulations.
Provide customers with ongoing technical support.
Advise customers on product usage to improve production.
Inform customers about issues related to responsible use and disposal of products, such as waste reduction or product or byproduct recycling or disposal.
Prepare and submit sales contracts for orders.
Maintain customer records, using automated systems.
Complete expense reports, sales reports, or other paperwork.
Verify that delivery schedules meet project deadlines.
Arrange for installation and testing of products or machinery.
Initiate sales campaigns to meet sales and production expectations.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Provide feedback to product design teams so that products can be tailored to clients' needs.
Collaborate with colleagues to exchange information, such as selling strategies or marketing information.
Consult with engineers regarding technical problems with products.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Emphasize product features, based on analyses of customers' needs and on technical knowledge of product capabilities and limitations.
Inform customers of estimated delivery schedules, service contracts, warranties, or other information pertaining to purchased products.
Present information to customers about the energy efficiency or environmental impact of scientific or technical products.
Quote prices, credit terms, or other bid specifications.
Compute customer's installation or production costs and estimate savings from new services, products, or equipment.
Negotiate prices or terms of sales or service agreements.
Visit establishments to evaluate needs or to promote product or service sales.
Answer customers' questions about products, prices, availability, or credit terms.
Prepare sales presentations or proposals to explain product specifications or applications.
Identify prospective customers, using business directories, leads from existing clients, participation in organizations, or trade show or conference attendance.
Verify accuracy of materials lists.
Verify customer credit ratings.
Study documentation or other information for new scientific or technical products.
Stock or distribute resources, such as samples or promotional or educational materials.
Attend sales or trade meetings or read related publications to obtain information about market conditions, business trends, environmental regulations, or industry developments.
Visit establishments, such as pharmacies, to determine product sales.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Management of Financial Resources
skills.def: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Google Workspace software, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Customer relationship management CRM software
skills.def: Software to manage customer interactions. Examples: Act!, ActionWare, AdTrack Customer Acquisition Management CAM, AMG Teleran SalesInSync.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: IBM Notes, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, FileMaker Pro, Microsoft Access, Oracle Database.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Infor ERP SyteLine, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite ERP, Oracle Fusion Applications.
